newsitem.title: CANADA: Pacific Forest calls for bids by June 16.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Forest calls for bids by June 16.

text.p: Pacific Forest Products Ltd, which put itself up for sale last month, said Wednesday it set a deadline for final bids of June 16.
Pacific Forest and 53 percent owner Avenor Inc on Montreal announced they were seeking a buyer and also considering turning the lumber company into a timberland income fund.
Paul Gagne, chief executive of Avenor and chairman of Pacific Forest, told the Pacific Forest annual meeting that confidential information has been mailed out to potential bidders.
Bidders have been told to submit non-binding offers by May 12 after which they will have access to more Pacific Forest information and be able to tour its operations.
Final offers are then due by June 16.
At the same time, the company is compiling information that would be necessary for the launch of the timberland income fund.

Gagne said an independent committee of the board would review all offers before they are put to the full board. Another independent committee of directors has been established to express an opinion on fairness of any decision.

Pacific Forest chief executive Sandy Fulton told reporters that a "couple dozen" Canadian and U.S. companies were sent the initial information package on the company. "I expect a lot of attention," he said.
The move reflects a decision by Avenor to realize value from its investment in Pacific Forest and focus on its pulp and paper business in eastern Canada, he said.

Fulton said Pacific Forest is in strong shape and noted a big increase in first-quarter earnings reported Tuesday. He projected softer lumber and saw log prices in the next few months followed by stronger prices later in the year.
Pulp log prices were showing some sign of improvement but chip prices look likely to remain depressed, he said.

Fulton said he was optimistic that the British Columbia government will grant forest companies some cost relief on their logging operations. The province and forest industry have been negotiating for months on potential measures to lower costs and increase employment in the sector.
